says: In next/, the L14 secrets law printed the resolved settings with a plain JSON.stringify, and the first byte-size setting, mail.chunk, decodes to a bigint, so the law threw before it searched anything. The product was right: the recorded snapshot holds the byte size as its text, and nothing in the product prints the decoded values as JSON. Fixed in the same pull request: the law prints a bigint as its digits, through one helper it also uses for spans and the error, and still searches every value. Three plants, each run once and undone, turned it red: the secret leaked into a resolved value, into a span beside the bigint value, and into the error message.
proof: vitest on Snapshot.test.ts at this head: `TypeError: Do not know how to serialize a BigInt` at Snapshot.test.ts:468:31, the same as CI run 43723346561, leg next (3).
cost: The secrets law for settings stopped checking anything the day the first byte-size setting landed, and it would stay red on every full run.
